nodes.name: NiFeOOH Construction via Corrosion Engineering
nodes.procedure: Fe foam was used as the current collector and Fe source. A Ni_xFe_yOOH substrate (denoted as NiFe) was constructed through corrosion engineering on ordered NiFe-based nanoarrays.
nodes.source_text: Fe foam was used as the current collector and Fe source. A Ni_xFe_yOOH substrate (denoted as NiFe) was constructed through corrosion engineering. ordered NiFe-based nanoarrays provide a suitable substrate

nodes.name: Ru Solution Impregnation
nodes.procedure: Various metals were subsequently loaded onto the NiFe substrate via solution impregnation, leading to the construction of large-scale catalyst electrodes. The concentration of Ru in the impregnation solution was systematically varied to optimize catalytic activity. Systematic adjustments revealed that 10 mmol/L Ru concentration yielded optimal performance.

nodes.source_text: The LSV curves in Figure 4a show that Ru-NiFe has excellent catalytic activity, with the overpotential at 10mAcm⁻² being 5mV... Ru-NiFe exhibits a Tafel slope of 58.2mVdec⁻¹ (Figure 4c)... can operate stably for more than 1000h... at a large current density of 500mAcm⁻² (Figure 4e). An error line chart (Figure 2e) further illustrates that the standard deviation of overpotentials increases slightly from 0.74mV at 10mAcm⁻² to 2.28mV at 300mAcm⁻².

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show the NiFe substrate mainly presented in the structure of interlaced nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images in Figure S5 comprehensively demonstrate that the NiFe substrate is mainly presented in the structure of interlaced nanosheets.

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution TEM image confirms NiFe exists in the form of ultrathin nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution transmission electron microscopy (TEM) image further confirmed that NiFe exists in the form of ultrathin nanosheets (Figure 3a).

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM images display Ru anchored on the NiFe substrate surface as clusters.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-angle annular dark field-scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) images display that Ru was anchored on the NiFe substrate surface as clusters (Figure 3b,c).

nodes.characterization_summary: Elemental mapping confirms Ru element uniformly distributed with Ni, Fe, and O elements, no local aggregation of Ru.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The corresponding elemental mapping confirms that the Ru element was uniformly distributed with the Ni, Fe, and O elements, and no local aggregation of Ru can be observed (Figure 3d).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD pattern showed only FeOOH (PDF #76-2301) characteristic peaks, without Ru peaks, indicating amorphous Ru clusters.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD pattern (Figure S6) showed only FeOOH (PDF #76-2301) characteristic peaks, without Ru peaks, indicating amorphous Ru clusters.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS of Ru 3p revealed peaks at 463.6 and 485.5 eV for Ru 3p3/2 and Ru 3p1/2 between Ru(0) and Ru(IV), confirming Ru introduction. Ni 2p XPS spectra showed Ni²⁺ at 855.5 eV with shakeup satellites, while Fe 2p spectra displayed Fe³⁺ peaks at 711.4 and 725.1 eV. The slight positive shift of Fe 2p3/2 in Ru-NiFe relative to NiFe suggests increased Fe oxidation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XPS of Ru 3p revealed peaks at 463.6 and 485.5 eV for Ru 3p3/2 and Ru 3p1/2, between Ru (0) and Ru (IV), confirming Ru introduction (Figure S7a). Ni 2p XPS spectra showed Ni²⁺ at 855.5 eV with shakeup satellites, while Fe 2p spectra displayed Fe³⁺ peaks at 711.4 and 725.1 eV (Figure S7b,c).

nodes.characterization_summary: XANES spectra of Ru K-edge show the absorption edge of Ru in Ru-NiFe lies between Ru foil and RuO₂, closer to RuO₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 3e, the absorption edge of Ru in Ru-NiFe lies between Ru foil and RuO₂, closer to RuO₂, indicating its oxidation state is similar to RuO₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fourier-transformed EXAFS spectra of Ru K-edge show peaks at 1.38 and 2.7 Å assigned to Ru-O and Ru-O-M (Ni/Fe) scattering paths. Model-based fitting confirms each Ru atom is coordinated with 4.6±0.8 oxygen atoms, with 1.7±1 Ru-O bonded to nearby metal (Ni/Fe).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fourier transforms of the phase-uncorrected EXAFS for Ru-NiFe (Figure 3f) show distinct peaks at 1.38 and 2.7Å assigned to Ru-O and Ru-O-M (Ni/Fe) scattering paths... Model-based EXAFS fitting (Table S1) confirms each Ru atom is coordinated with 4.6±0.8 oxygen atoms, with 1.7±1 Ru-O bonded to nearby metal (Ni/Fe).

nodes.characterization_summary: Mass fraction of Ru, Ni, and Fe in Ru-NiFe is 2.73%, 11.5%, and 81.2%, respectively.
nodes.evidence_snippet: According to the inductively coupled plasma-mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) results, the mass fraction of Ru, Ni, and Fe in Ru-NiFe is 2.73%, 11.5%, and 81.2%, respectively (Figure S9a).

nodes.characterization_summary: WT EXAFS of Ru K-edge shows Ru-O-M scattering peak lies left of Ru-O-Ru scattering in RuO₂, indicating M (Ni/Fe) has smaller atomic number than Ru, confirming Ru clusters bond to NiFe substrate via Ru-O-M bridges.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Ru-NiFe, the Ru-O-M scattering peak lies left of Ru-O-Ru scattering in RuO₂, indicating M has a smaller atomic number than Ru (Figure 3g).
